units.title: Bed mobility and pivot transfers
units.summary: Bed Mobility • Bridging • Moving across the bed • Upward movement / Downward movement Pivot Transfers If patient is able to weight bearing safely on at least one of the lower extremities & able to follow instructions, it is suitable to use pivot transfers. In pivot transfers, the primary action occurs through the feet. • Moving the hip forward • Foot position – flat on the floor, and places posterior • Trunk flexion • Using a gait belt if needed 3. Therapist Position: • In front of the patient • With hip & knee flexed • Wide Base of support

units.title: Conditions with precautions
units.summary: Conditions with Precautions Total hip replacement (THR) OR dislocated hip • DON’T place affected side in Cross leg position (flex+ adducted+ medial rotated) OR flexion > 90° 90° • maintain affected side in semi- reclining position & abduction during side transfer • Use of abduction pillow if prescribed • Especially within the first 2 weeks after surgery Conditions with Precautions Hemiplegia /Stroke • Avoid PULLING the hemiplegic (weakened) side (esp FLACCID/ HYPOTONIA ) as this may lead to joint dislocation • NOT to lie/ roll on AFFECTED shoulder due to pain & discomfort Conditions with Precautions Spinal cord injury • Suggest LOGROLL & avoid rotational force logroll • Chronic cases, cautious NOT to fracture long bones of lower limbs or vertebrates due to osteoporosis “LOGROLL” i.e. simultaneously rolling the entire body Conditions with Precautions Presence of pressure ulcers • avoid sliding (shearing force) as create friction that disrupts healing process • encourage to elevate body during transfer

units.title: Standard wheelchairs and fitting
units.summary: Wheelchair • More than simply a chair on wheels, a wheelchair (WC) is a postural support system on a mobility base. • While in use, this dynamic seating environment allows patient to achieve stability, controlled mobility, and skill in daily function. How to choose a suitable wheelchair for a patient? • Type of wheelchair: • lightweight transport, for patient that pushed by others • Standard wheelchairs with larger rear wheels, for self propelled patient • Sport • Reclining • Electric Standard Wheelchair - Postural Support Options 1.

units.title: Use of the wheelchair
units.summary: Using the wheelchair Opening: ➢ Push down and outward on the sides of the seat until fully opened Closing: ➢ Lift the footplates up. Grasp the front and back of the seat canvas and pull upwards. ➢ NOT to lift the detachable parts. Safety tips for using wheelchair ➢ Always LOCK the brakes when you leave the patient or when not being pushed. ➢ Avoid leaning forwards or bending to reach low objects ➢ Never stand on the footplates ➢ Use safety straps if provided (especially when going outdoors or for patient with poor sitting balance) ➢ Make sure: ➢ Feet safely on the footplates ➢ Elbows, all clothing, rugs or bags are tucked in safely.
